task.value:
Read who the department is against Identity's standard, and say whether it is enough to start work on. The standard has five points, and only five:
goal: the goal names what the department makes and for whom.
items: done-when is a list of items, and each item says how it is checked.
rules: every rule is tagged go, ask, refuse or always.
owner, budget: the department has an owner and a budget.
invented: nothing is invented; a fact the owner did not give is marked to confirm, never stated. Be brief.

Recognise, in plain words, what kind of words the owner has given. There are five kinds, and only five:
task: "do X for me". query: "tell me Y". directive: "from now on, do Z", a standing change to how the department works or to its goal. feedback: "that was wrong", about work already made. new-idea: "I want a new capability", something the department cannot do today.

guidance.value: high: a reader could be harmed or misled by it. At most three findings.

text.value: In this version the choice is made by code, not by words its agent reads: a step whose answers agree run after run is proposed one rung up, to a checklist or to code, and is tried beside the old way first; a step that keeps missing is proposed one rung down. Every move goes to Priority first, and Adaptation never applies one itself. Prefer a checklist to code when both would serve.
